The relevant facts for the disposal of this Rule, in short, are that the petitioner Ali Azam as plaintiff instituted the instant suit for declaration that the defendant is his benamder in respect of the land as described in the schedule of the plaint. They are full brothers. The plaintiff joined in service in 1956. On the other hand, the defendant joined in 1972. Their father served in a Sub-Registrar's office. He had two wives, two sons and two daughters by his first wife and one son and two daughters by his second wife. He was a resident of village Mokimpar. After erosion of property in the river, their father took shelter in the house of his elder brother at village Shyampur in 1950. He had no property. The plaintiff gave in marriage of his sisters and bore all the educational expenditures of younger brother from his earnings. The plaintiff's father retired, from his service in 1968. The plaintiff purchased 2.50 acre of land as described in the schedule 'Ka' of the plaint from one Yunus Mia by a kabala deed dated 4-4-1962 at consideration of Taka 1,000. He also purchased 1.25 acre of land from Momtaz and others by another kabala deed dated 6-4-1964 at consideration of Taka 500. He again purchased 2.86-1/2 acres of land from one Amar Krishna Routh and others by a kabala deed dated 10-11-1969 at consideration of Taka 1500. He also purchased 1.64 acre of land from one Amyo Prova Routh by another kabala deed dated 12-1-1970 at a consideration of Taka 500. He himself purchased the stamp papers of those kabala deeds and paid considerations. The defendant did not pay any consideration and registration cost for those four kabala deeds. At the time of purchase of those lands, the defendant was unemployed. He was a simple name lender of the plaintiff. The plaintiff mutated his name in the khatian and has been paying rent to the Government. Recently, the defendant claimed title in the suit land and, as such, the plaintiff filed the instant suit. 

 7. Mr Abul Kalam Chowdhury, the learned. Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party, submits that the instant transactions were not benami transactions and the suit in its present form was not maintainable. He further submits that some of the witnesses of plaintiff, particularly PW 9 in his evidence, admitted that both the parties have been possessing the suit land. He further submits that although the title documents of the land had been produced by the plaintiff but the same is not unnatural because the plaintiff is the full brother of the defendant. As the defendant has been serving as an officer of Trading Corporation of Bangladesh, so naturally, the title documents are to be kept in the custody of his full brother who has been living in his paternal house. It is evident that at the time of recent survey operation, the plaintiff brought the title documents from, he defendant in order to record their name in the khatian. He further submits that the plaintiff failed to prove motive of purchase of the suit land in the benami of the defendant. He further submits that the plaintiff and the defendant are full brothers and they purchased the suit land from the money given by their mother, father and from their own funds. That is, the lements of banani transaction are not present in the instant case. In such view of the matter, the learned appellate Court rightly dismissed the suit reversing the judgment and decree of the trial Court. 

 15. On the other hand, from the Exhibit G-1, it appears that the suit land has been recorded in the name of both the brothers, that is the plaintiff allowed the defendant to record his name in the khatian.
